newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin orders full reorganisation of government.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin orders full reorganisation of government.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin ordered a full reorganisation of the government on Tuesday, effectively telling Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and his first deputy Anatoly Chubais to form a new cabinet.

A Yeltsin decree published by his press service said the president had accepted Chernomyrdin's proposal to restructure the government which would now have only one first deputy prime minister instead of four.
It was clear that this post would be held by Chubais, appointed only last Friday. Chief government spokesman Igor Shabdurasulov confirmed this in an interview with Itar-Tass news agency.

The decree said the number of deputy prime ministers would be cut from the current figure of nine. The number of ministries -- and of ministers -- would also be cut and some of the ministries reorganised.
The decree did not give any names and did not order a formal resignation of the government.
Chernomyrdin was given a week to present a list of personnel changes in the government.

Yeltsin said last Thursday he would reorganise the government, bringing in "competent and energetic" people. The next day he appointed his loyal ally, liberal Chubais, to the post of first deputy prime minister.
